items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: Nat did it, Ella did it, but no one did it like Billy Strayhorn.

ctx.x: You liked that, that was a tough one. You know, to this very day, I'm supposed to know a lot of songs, you know, a bass player where I've been playing for a thousand years, I think I know a lot of tunes and anybody comesand sits down and says what do you want to play, a piano player, what do you want to play, he says I'd like to play 'Lush Life', I get scared to death, because even though I learned it a million times and played it with some wonderful people like --
Well, he was the only one that could play it and get something out of it. Billy, what's his name, the guy that died. Nat Cole. Nat did it, Ella did it, but no one did it like Billy Strayhorn.
The change is unbelievable. I freeze up because they're not just the usual run of things and I'm always afraid of it. Okay. I played it before but I don't think I know it now. Worried to death.
